llmJudgeRequirements.description: Store uses `persist` with `createJSONStorage(() => AsyncStorage)` and persists only token state
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: persist config uses only `name` and `partialize` — no `storage: createJSONStorage(() => AsyncStorage)` is present. AsyncStorage is listed as a dependency but never imported or wired into the store.
evidence: sessionStore: persist({...}, { name: TOKEN_KEY, partialize: ... }) — no storage field

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Store state includes `hasHydrated` `token` `profileStatus` `profileName` and hydration setter action
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: `hasHydrated`, `token`, and a hydration setter are present, but `profileStatus` and `profileName` as discrete fields are absent. Profile is stored as a nested `profile` object, not as separate `profileStatus`/`profileName` fields. There is no dedicated `setHasHydrated` action.
evidence: SessionState interface has `profile: { firstName; lastName } | null` and `hasHydrated: boolean`, but no `profileStatus` or `profileName` fields

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Login action performs `POST` request to auth login endpoint and writes returned token into store
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: login action POSTs to `https://dummyjson.com/auth/login` and writes `data.accessToken || data.token` into store via `set({ token: accessToken })`.
evidence: sessionStore login: fetch('https://dummyjson.com/auth/login', { method: 'POST', ... }); set({ token: accessToken })

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Profile fetch request sends `Authorization` bearer header built from persisted token
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: fetchProfile reads token from store and sends `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` header in the request to the profile endpoint.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: onRehydrateStorage sets hydrated flag in success and error paths and reloads profile when token exists
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: onRehydrateStorage callback references `set` and `get` from outer closure, but those identifiers are not in scope inside `onRehydrateStorage` (it is outside the `create` callback). The success path also has a logic bug: `state?.hasHydrated ? null : set({ hasHydrated: true })` — hasHydrated is always false on rehydration so the ternary always calls set, but the structure is incorrect. More critically, the error path (second argument to onRehydrateStorage for handling errors) is never handled.
evidence: onRehydrateStorage: () => (state) => { state?.hasHydrated ? null : set(...) — set/get are out of scope; no (state, error) error path handler }

llmJudgeRequirements.description: UI renders hydration loading branch when `hasHydrated` is false
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: App.tsx renders a loading view when `!hasHydrated` is true.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: UI renders profile loading branch when token exists and `profileStatus` is loading
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: UI does not have a dedicated branch that checks `token && profileStatus === 'loading'`. It uses a generic `isLoading` flag rendered as a text element regardless of auth state, not a distinct branch gated on token existence and a `profileStatus` field.
evidence: App.tsx: {isLoading && <Text>Loading...</Text>} — no branch conditional on `token` and `profileStatus`
